passage: The delegates never voted on the text that their five-member committee first circulated. That version was marked up during three weeks of floor debate, returned to the committee, and recirculated twice before the final vote, by which point about a third of its clauses had been rewritten. Historians who quote the first version as though it were the constitution itself are therefore confusing the committee's early ______ with the document the delegates actually adopted.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: The word "draft" fits because the first version was a complete proposed text that was then debated, revised, and recirculated before anything was adopted. "Digest" fails because a digest summarizes some other text, while the first version was the proposed text itself. "Gloss" fails because a gloss is commentary on a text, not the text under debate. "Excerpt" fails because the passage describes a whole version whose clauses were later rewritten, not a portion taken from a larger document.
